Board D's own board entry states 'every row sourceUrl to governing-body domain', which the data does not support.

findings.title: High-confidence predictions contain form/injury claims contradicted by, or absent from, official sources
findings.detail: NHL01 says the Sharks were 0-4 on their road trip — the NHL preview lists them 4-4-1. NHL06 says Boston were 1-3 on a Texas swing and missing Marchand — the NHL preview lists Boston 7-2-0 and Marchand is not a Bruin. EL02 inverts the EuroLeague records (press lists Efes 2-4, Beşiktaş 3-3), labels 20:30 local as CET, names a venue that disagrees with the broadcaster listing and contains an unedited self-correction ('blowout of Efes? Actually…'). MLB01 cites a 'seven-game ALCS' — it was six games. RL01 describes a 'Pacific Championships Australia v NZ Oct 25 Brisbane' that does not exist in 2026 (RLWC; 25 Oct Brisbane is Australia v Fiji). The remaining rows carry statistics (home records, averages, streaks) that appear on none of the linked sources. Recommend: withdraw or rewrite these predictions from official pages, or move the rows to the hub's Flagged page.

findings.title: Fixture fields that disagree with the governing body

CRK05 dates the final 29 Oct (PCB: 31 Oct; 29 Oct is Sri Lanka v England). MLB03 venue reads 'George M. Steinbrenner Field / …' (MLB: Rays host at Tropicana Field). EL02 time '20:30 CET' is 20:30 Istanbul time = 17:30 CET.

findings.title: Hub 'entries' that are not matches
findings.detail: The brief asks for a list of matches. About half of the hub's 66 entries are tournaments, round summaries, completed events used 'for form', off-season notes ('AFL Off-Season — No scheduled matches') or qualification news ('eight clubs confirmed'). Several still carry a pick and confidence (e.g. ATP01 'Medium' with a Kalshi prediction-market percentage; BDM02 'High' outright). These should either be expanded to individual matches with official fixture links or be moved off the match table.

findings.title: Row-level source is OLBG only; confidence derives from tipster consensus
findings.detail: Each Build B row links the OLBG event page as its sole source; only the 9 high-confidence rows add official fact links inside their predictions. The 'own line' is a shrunken transform of the OLBG tip percentage (p = (n·p_c + 1)/(n+2)), so B's probabilities and confidence bands are a function of OLBG tipster votes rather than independently verified form. Build B discloses this in its methodology; it is recorded here because the brief asks for an official link on every row and for lines originated by us.

findings.title: Same fixture, opposite match-winner picks in different builds
findings.detail: 93 fixtures appear in two or more of builds A, C, D, E, G; in 10 the builds name different match winners. Most notable: Build C rates Charlotte Hornets a HIGH-confidence pick while Build A picks Brooklyn (low). Because each build uses a different model and input snapshot this is expected, but a reader of the portal sees contradictory picks for the same game with no reconciliation. See the Cross-build page for all overlaps.

findings.detail: COORDINATION.md says each session edits only its claimed scope and logs requests for other boards' files. Commit cf9f024 (labelled 'Board E: arena/4359d6a4-olbg4') rewrote Build A's data file — dropping the two Gaelic football rows (in scope; Galway final re-verified on galwaygaa.ie), three greyhound rows, the golf row and the motor-racing row — replaced Build A's 12 hand-written predictions with 25 templated ones, deleted four of Build A's sport pages, and overwrote data/predictions.json, which was Build B's file (schema olbg4.predictions/1 with per-claim source URLs). Build B's own HTML pages still show its original write-ups, so the site and the data layer now disagree. The pre-overwrite files are recoverable from git (5918922:data/rows.json, 5918922:data/predictions.json, 5918922:docs/…). Recommend the integration owner restore them or Board A/B confirm the change.

findings.title: Templated, repetitive predictions; one names the wrong opponent
findings.detail: The brief asks for unique, non-robotic predictions that name the team/player, current form and recent match history. In the rewritten data/rows.json, 13 of 25 high-confidence predictions open with the identical sentence 'PDC tour seeding points accumulated over the season provide a reliable indicator…' and contain no form or result at all; the NHL ones share a single template ('X entered this match with a points percentage of … compared to Y's …., reflecting a significant regular-season strength differential'), including a '.,' punctuation artefact. The Boston Bruins v Nashville Predators row's prediction compares Boston with the San Jose Sharks — the opponent from a different fixture. The docs/index.html high-confidence table was regenerated from this file, so the published Build A landing page now shows these texts. The original 12 write-ups (66+ words, individually written) are in git at 5918922.
